pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: `f := r.(*os.File)` versus `f, ok := r.(*os.File)` — what happens in each when `r` does not hold a `*os.File`, and when is the first form acceptable?
expected_points: the single-value form panics on mismatch
the comma-ok form sets ok to false and f to the zero value, never panicking
single-value is only right when the dynamic type is a guaranteed invariant, so being wrong should crash loudly

questions.prompt: Sketch a type switch over `v any` that handles string and int differently. What type does `v` have inside each case, and does `case int` match an `int64`?
expected_points: switch v := v.(type) with one case per type plus default
inside each case v has that case's concrete type
matching is exact — int64 does not match case int; it falls to default

questions.prompt: Your caller needs to know (a) whether a lookup failed with ErrNotFound, and (b) which field a *ValidationError complained about. Which of errors.Is / errors.As fits each, and why?
expected_points: errors.Is for (a): identity check against a sentinel value, yes/no answer
errors.As for (b): matches by type and copies the match out so its fields are readable
Is takes a value to compare, As takes a pointer to a variable of the error type (e.g. &ve)

questions.prompt: Why does `errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound)` still work after the error was wrapped twice with fmt.Errorf — and what would change if one layer had used %v instead of %w?
expected_points: %w makes the returned error carry an Unwrap() error method pointing at the wrapped error
repeated wrapping forms a chain; Is and As walk it by calling Unwrap until a match or the end
%v produces the same message but no Unwrap link — the chain is severed and Is/As stop finding the cause

questions.prompt: A codebase type-switches over Circle/Rect in five different files to compute areas. Why is that a design smell, and what is the idiomatic fix?
expected_points: adding a new type means finding and extending every switch; missing one fails silently
the behavior belongs on the types: add an Area() method to the interface and let each type implement it
type switches are fine at boundaries over types you don't control (fmt-style formatting, decoding, error inspection)

questions.prompt: You can assert to an interface type too: `s, ok := v.(fmt.Stringer)`. What question does that ask, and where does the standard library use this trick?
expected_points: it asks whether the dynamic type implements the interface, not whether it equals a specific type
behavior discovery for optional abilities
e.g. fmt checks for Stringer; io.Copy checks for WriterTo/ReaderFrom to take a fast path

questions.prompt: Designing a new package: when do you export a sentinel error and when a custom error type? What does each commit you to?
expected_points: sentinel when callers only need yes/no on a specific failure
error type when the failure carries data callers must read
an exported type's fields become API surface — a bigger long-term commitment than a sentinel
